briefHtml:
NAV and the tape

  • NAV S$10,193,410 · reported -0.60% · real day move ≈ -0.09% (S$-9,052 vs Friday's final 10,202,462). NAV level authoritative; Friday's NAV was restated down 0.14% after the morning snapshot.
  • Biggest mover in the book's world: AMD -8.75% Friday as the post-Huang chip selloff rolled on; NVDA -2.01% to $162.85 (-12% on the week, below $4tn) into earnings TOMORROW (Tue 17 Nov) — first print of the post-Huang era, interim CEO Colette Kress.
  • The one thing: the 10y closed 5.15% Friday (+5bp, high 5.17%) — the 5.20% Defense gate is 5bp away, the closest yet, with PPI at 6.5% y/y (hottest since Nov 2022) keeping a December hike ~90% locked. Gate decision lands between NVDA Tuesday and Anthropic's ~$1.4tn IPO Thursday.
  • All 8 watcher riskFlags are stale-baseline artifacts: real Friday moves — Xiaomi -3.74% (flag -5.0%), GDX -0.24% (flag -6.8%), SILJ ≈-1.5% (flag -7.6%), SLVP -1.20% (flag -7.6%), Tencent -3.06% (flag -7.9% = its exact 5-day move), CDL ≈+0.4% (flag -11.0%, wrong sign), silver futures -1.89% (flag -4.8%). listedChgPct -3.46% is inconsistent with NAV -0.09%.
  • Metals at support: gold $3,878.70 — sitting ON its 52-week low ($3,875.36); silver spot ~$48.97, second week below $50. Silver line now ≈1.99x — effectively AT 2x.
  • SMIC sell-the-news on a strong print: spiked to HK$52.30 (+7.3%), closed 48.52 -0.45%; Q3 gross margin 29.9% crushed the 26–28% guide, utilisation 97.3%, Q4 guided +4–6% q/q. AMAT verified: Q4 revenue $10.41bn +53%, Q1 guide $11.1bn far above consensus; stock -2.8% Friday.

Flag integrity

  • riskFlags: EIGHT critical — every magnitude overstated (verification table in the brief). Tencent's -7.9% exactly matches its 5-day move: the watcher is printing multi-day moves as daily.
  • No position had a real -5% Friday; the Asia-tech and metals complex DID fall hard over the week — direction right, magnitude wrong.
  • L46.SI (Lum Chang): Yahoo 404, 33rd consecutive session.
  • listedChgPct -3.46% fails the NAV cross-check (NAV -0.09%); treat as stale too.

Insider trades (last 7 days)

  • None found. SGX links API 404 for a fourth consecutive trading day — web sweep only.
  • Wing Tai: nothing newer than the 4 Nov Form 1 — pause now six trading sessions (5, 6, 10, 11, 12, 13 Nov).
  • DBS, Fraser and Neave, VICOM, Straits Trading, City Developments, UOL, Ho Bee, Seatrium, YZJ, Singtel, Keppel REIT; HK names Tencent, SMIC, Xiaomi: none found. US sleeve is ETFs — no insider filings exist.

Congress trades (STOCK Act)

  • 88 trades disclosed Nov 7–14 (45 buys / 43 sells) — one lawmaker made 58 of them.
  • CA-31 (House, D), filed 11 Nov: SOLD NVDA on 20 Oct — three weeks before the Huang scandal broke; sold Tokyo Electron twice; bought CSCO, META, ServiceNow, Moderna, Lumentum.
  • OH-2 (House, R), filed 13 Nov: 19-row rotation — bought AVGO, LRCX, GOOGL x2, Eaton x2, ATandT x2; sold Visa x2, Eli Lilly x2, Kroger x2, Amgen x2, PG, Home Depot (trades 3–5 Nov).
  • NJ-5 (House, D), filed 6 Nov: bought AMAT on 26 Oct — two weeks before its +53% revenue print.
  • GA-12 (House, R), filed 12 Nov: bought two US Treasury notes ($15,001–50,000 each, 2 Oct). WV (Senate, R), filed 4 Nov: sold AAPL, META, MSFT, Zoetis (21 Oct).

Trump and policy watch (weekend + 48h)

  • NVDA scandal is now a China-policy storm: bipartisan push (Johnson + Jeffries backing) to attach tougher AI-chip export curbs on China to the NDAA before year-end; Wyden and Neal opened a probe into the H200 approve-and-tax deal; Lutnick testifies 10 Dec. The Hill
  • Megaspeed — the Singapore angle: Bessent said Treasury, Defense, State and USTR all wanted the Singapore-based firm on the Entity List for months; Commerce BIS stalled. Export-diversion scrutiny of SG intermediaries intensifies. CBS
  • China extended the Busan truce ~2 months to 10 Jan 2027 — rare-earth, battery and graphite export-control suspensions, US-vessel port fees, Hanwha countermeasures; matches USTR's 6 Nov ships-301 extension. Snapback risk defused for now. Beijing warned against new chip controls. China Briefing
  • PPI 6.5% y/y — hottest since Nov 2022 (+0.3% m/m, cooler than feared); December hike ~90% priced; 10y 5.15%, 2y 4.88% (+42bp in a week — bear flattener). Yahoo
  • Anthropic IPO week: pricing Wed 18 Nov, first trade Thu 19 Nov as ANT — 825m shares at $70–78 (~$1.4tn fully diluted); FT: bankers weighing pricing ABOVE $78 on heavy demand; ~20% retail; TSMC taking $500m; run-rate revenue ~$81bn. Yahoo
  • Oil surplus signal: IEA sees the oil market in surplus for the first time since the war began; Brent ~$96 posted a second straight weekly decline despite Trump's Iran-deal dismissal. Global Oil Shock

Risk

  • Silver line: 1,777 oz x $48.97 x 1.2878 ≈ S$112,064 collateral vs S$56,240 loan → equity ≈ S$55,824 (-S$2.0k d/d), ratio ≈ 1.99x — AT the 2x line; a further ~2% silver drop pushes it through.
  • Duration gate at 5bp: 10y 5.15% vs 5.20% gate, with NVDA (Tue) and Anthropic (Thu) binaries able to gap yields either way — gate order must be staged and executable.
  • NVDA earnings tomorrow: first print without Huang, mid-scandal, after a -12% week; AI-sleeve correlations go to 1 on a miss.
  • NDAA chip-curb tail hits the China/HK tech sleeve; partially offset by the Busan extension to January.
  • Real assets bleeding into support: gold ON its 52-week low, silver ~$49, SILJ YTD -12% — the 20% target sleeve is the book's biggest mark-to-market drag.
  • Concentration and FX: ~35% of net worth non-SGD at USDSGD 1.2878; unlisted plus property dominate; CDL stabilised Friday (+0.4%).

Alpha — signals, not advice (~62% of the liquid book idle cash)

  • TLT / Defense sleeve: 10y 5.15%, gate 5.20% just 5bp away — closest yet. Signal: alert armed; deploy first tranche AT 5.20%; let any event-driven overshoot (5.25%+) be the better fill. The 2y at 4.88% says the market is doing the Fed's work.
  • SMIC (0981.HK): GM 29.9% crushed guidance, Q4 accelerating, yet faded +7.3% → -0.45% Friday. Signal: staged-entry trigger (hold above ~HK$46–47) is MET at 48.52; the fade is a better price than Thursday's chase. Size in tranches; December NDAA debate is the explicit risk budget.
  • Gold / miners (Real assets): gold ON its 52-week low with GDX flat Friday — downside momentum exhausting at support. Signal: UNLEVERED sleeve only (silver line at ~1.99x gets nothing): if gold holds 3,850–3,875 through the NVDA/Anthropic gauntlet, begin the first accumulation tranche toward the 20% target; a clean break below 3,850 defers it.

trumpWatch.title: NVDA scandal becomes a China-policy storm: chip curbs headed for the NDAA
trumpWatch.detail: Bipartisan lawmakers backed by Speaker Johnson and incoming-speaker Jeffries are pushing tougher AI-chip export curbs on China, possibly attached to the must-pass NDAA before year-end. Wyden and Neal opened a probe into Trump's approve-and-tax H200 deal (25% revenue cut) and ordered Commerce Secretary Lutnick to preserve records; Lutnick testifies to Senate Banking on 10 Dec.

trumpWatch.title: Megaspeed fight puts Singapore in the export-diversion spotlight
trumpWatch.detail: Treasury Secretary Bessent said on CNBC Friday that Treasury, Defense, State and USTR all supported adding Singapore-based Megaspeed to the Entity List 'for months' while Commerce BIS stalled. Expect tighter scrutiny of Singapore-based chip intermediaries; Beijing calls the Huang allegations a pretext for a technological blockade.

trumpWatch.title: China extended the Busan truce ~2 months to 10 Jan 2027
trumpWatch.detail: MOFCOM/GAC rolled over suspensions of rare-earth, lithium-battery and graphite export controls, US-vessel port fees and Hanwha countermeasures on 9 Nov, matching USTR's 6 Nov ships-301 extension. The tariff-snapback risk flagged last week is defused for now; direct relief for the China/HK tech sleeve.

trumpWatch.title: PPI 6.5% y/y — hottest since Nov 2022; December hike ~90% locked
trumpWatch.detail: October PPI rose 0.3% m/m (cooler than the 0.4% expected) but the annual rate hit 6.5%, the largest since Nov 2022. 10y closed 5.15% Friday (+5bp, high 5.17%), 2y 4.88% (+42bp in a week) — a bear flattener doing the Fed's work. The 5.20% duration gate is 5bp away.

trumpWatch.title: Anthropic IPO week: pricing Wed, trading Thu as ANT
trumpWatch.detail: 825m Class A shares at $70–78 (~$1.4tn fully diluted at the top) plus a $26bn concurrent placement; the institutional book was covered on day one and FT reports bankers are weighing pricing above $78. Up to 20% retail; TSMC is taking $500m at the IPO price. Run-rate revenue ~$81bn as of 31 Oct. NVDA earnings Tuesday opens the same AI-trade test.

trumpWatch.title: IEA: oil market in surplus for the first time since the war began
trumpWatch.detail: Brent (~$96) posted a second straight weekly decline and WTI settled $88.56 despite Trump's Thursday dismissal of an immediate Iran deal; US crude stocks rose 4.7m barrels. The oil-driven inflation impulse is fading even as PPI prints hot.
